classification.difficultyReason: Use scaffolded equal-radius angle expressions to establish a general right-angle result, transfer it to another circumference point and combine that proof with a parallel-line angle calculation.

content.prompt: $O$ is the centre of the circle shown opposite.

spec.sourceRegion: Geometry challenge, Question 3, lower-right circle diagram
spec.description: Circle with diameter BC, centre O, circumference points A and D, and external point E. B, D and E are collinear; AB and EC are parallel. AO is dashed red and O is a red point. Ordinary source-blue geometry is rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: OA=OB=OC; B,O,C are collinear; B,D,E are collinear; AB is parallel to EC; alpha is angle ABC and beta is angle ACB. Coordinates construct the relationships without supplying numerical measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and auxiliary radius are visible; no answers or additional right-angle marks.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Let $\angle ABC$ be $\alpha$. Express $\angle AOC$ in terms of $\alpha$.

answer.worked:
$OA=OB$ because they are radii, so $\angle OAB=\angle ABO=\alpha$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB&=180^\circ-\alpha-\alpha\\\angle AOB&=180^\circ-2\alpha\end{align*}$$

Since $B$, $O$ and $C$ lie on a straight line,

$$\begin{align*}\angle AOC&=180^\circ-(180^\circ-2\alpha)\\\angle AOC&=2\alpha.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Let $\angle ACB$ be $\beta$. Express $\angle AOB$ in terms of $\beta$.

answer.worked:
$OA=OC$ because they are radii, so $\angle OAC=\angle ACO=\beta$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle AOC&=180^\circ-\beta-\beta\\\angle AOC&=180^\circ-2\beta\end{align*}$$

Since $B$, $O$ and $C$ lie on a straight line,

$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB&=180^\circ-(180^\circ-2\beta)\\\angle AOB&=2\beta.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Prove that $\triangle ABC$ is a right-angled triangle.

Hence, name two other right-angled triangles in the diagram.

answer.short:
$\angle BAC=90^\circ$. The other right-angled triangles are $\triangle BDC$ and $\triangle CDE$.

Use equal radii and the straight angle at $O$ to obtain $\alpha+\beta=90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
From parts a and b, the straight angle $BOC$ gives

$$\begin{align*}2\alpha+2\beta&=180^\circ\\\alpha+\beta&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$

By the angle sum of $\triangle ABC$,

$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=180^\circ-(\alpha+\beta)\\\angle BAC&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$

The same equal-radii argument for the circumference point $D$ gives $\angle BDC=90^\circ$, so $\triangle BDC$ is right-angled. Since $B$, $D$ and $E$ are collinear, $\angle CDE=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$, so $\triangle CDE$ is also right-angled.

answer.short:
$\angle ABD=115^\circ$.

Use the right angle at $D$ and $AB\parallel EC$.
answer.worked:
From part c, $\angle CDE=90^\circ$. In $\triangle CDE$,

$$\begin{align*}\angle CED&=180^\circ-90^\circ-25^\circ\\\angle CED&=65^\circ.\end{align*}$$

Since $B$, $D$ and $E$ are collinear, $\angle CEB=65^\circ$. The co-interior angles formed by $AB\parallel EC$ and transversal $BE$ sum to $180^\circ$:

$$\begin{align*}\angle ABD&=180^\circ-65^\circ\\\angle ABD&=115^\circ.\end{align*}$$
